correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation gives a signed derivative with positive weight confined below A-epsilon and negative weight confined above it. The negative-to-positive Gaussian-weighted ratio strictly increases from zero to infinity, proving one maximum; dominated convergence gives the half-floor limit. The mean-field sign threshold is algebraic, while an exact rational conditional-Jensen witness proves intermediate noise exceeds it with both endpoints below. The accompanying checker reproduces the rational inequalities; numerical quadrature is nonessential. No stochastic-lattice survival assertion is made.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparisons show the source treats quadratic small-noise mortality and a separate earlier source supplies deterministic mean-field growth. The new statement proves a global single-peak exact clipped-Gaussian death response and an explicit two-crossing ecological mean-field regime. General reentrance and Gaussian truncation are prior art, not claimed as new; a broader monotone-likelihood-ratio result may subsume a lemma but no decisive source-specific coverage was found.
residual_risks: The 1997 multiplicative-noise article was available only as an abstract; a general theorem from that literature may imply a scalar response property.
Published results on variation-diminishing Gaussian transforms or censored-normal fractional expectations could cover the scalar unimodality statement under different terminology.
The claim is mean-field only; treating it as an actual spatial survival transition would overstate the evidence.

value.rationale: The motivating work predicts mortality increases through a positive local quadratic correction, but its actual simulation truncates the Gaussian environmental quality. An exact global theorem shows this response eventually reverses, and a fixed rational ecological parameter set crosses the mean-field growth/decline boundary twice. This is a substantive qualitative phase classification of a motivated model, not a normalization or tiny numerical improvement; the distinction between mean-field and genuine spatial survival is explicit.
